core.title: What Makes Agent Memory Useful for Reliable Unanswerable Question Handling?
core.abstract: Reliable handling of unanswerable questions (UAQs) is critical for trustworthy LLM-based agents. Although memory is widely used in agent systems, its role in reliable UAQ handling remains unclear. We present a systematic study of agent memory for UAQ handling under a unified agentic RAG framework, evaluating four representative memory methods across three UAQ-related datasets and two base models.We find that memory can improve UAQ performance in some settings, but such gains are selective rather than universal and remain fragile under dataset shift. Interestingly, cross-model memory reuse is often more feasible than cross-dataset transfer, suggesting that shifts in answerability patterns pose a greater challenge to memory reuse than changes in the base model itself. We further find that UAQ gains are more strongly preserved through decision guidance than through trajectory shaping, and that memory effectiveness depends strongly on representation. In particular, procedural and rule-based memories often provide the most reliable support for UAQ handling, while memory composition is most effective when procedural guidance is combined with complementary behavioral signals. Overall, our findings suggest that reliable UAQ memory depends less on storing larger amounts of experience and more on preserving transferable behavioral guidance.

core.title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
core.abstract: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization, with 2-3 times AUC improvements over reinforcement-learning and genetic-algorithm baselines on the PMO benchmark and similar gains on protein-targeted docking benchmarks. We investigate whether these gains reflect genuine optimization or benchmark artifacts, by re-evaluating a representative LLM agent under controlled blinding protocols and against a trivial random-walk baseline. We find that on PMO at the 50-call budget, the agent’s apparent advantage collapses below classical baselines once task names and curated reference compounds are removed from its prompt; a 2 times 2 ablation shows that retrieval from a small reference dictionary, not iterative optimization, is the dominant driver of the headline number. On a new protein-targeted lead-optimization benchmark with an AutoDock Vina composite oracle, a single-edit halogen/methyl random-walk mutator outperforms the LLM agent, a graph-based GA, and a non-iterative GPT baseline on every aggregate metric—a property of the oracle landscape under tight budgets, not of LLM agents per se. We release both protocols (name-blinded PMO scoring; random-walk lower bound for Vina-based protein benchmarks) as standard sanity checks for future LLM-agent papers in molecular optimization.

core.title: WebTraveler: A Multi-Agent Framework for Continuous Exploration in Website Traversal
core.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as web-facing agents for information-seeking tasks over live websites. Many such tasks require multi-step in-site navigation and cross-page evidence aggregation, a setting known as web traversal. Existing LLM-based web agents, including recent explore–critic architectures, typically store interaction history as an ever-growing unstructured text trace and mix high-level planning with low-level page actions. This makes long-horizon behavior brittle, obscures the source of evidence, and often leads to redundant browsing or premature stopping. To mitigate these issues, we propose WebTraveler, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that separates high-level information-seeking planning from local web exploration and maintains a structured trajectory memory of decision-relevant signals. This design provides compact information interfaces for evidence sufficiency checking and webpage navigation, improving long-horizon stability and cross-page evidence aggregation. To obtain scalable supervision, we further introduce path-guided data synthesis, which uses executable navigation paths to collect trajectories, removes explicit path hints, and filters invalid samples through answer-consistency checks. Experiments show that WebTraveler consistently outperforms previous methods across LLM scales, especially on tasks requiring deeper navigation, with further gains from path-guided supervision. Moreover, WebTraveler also shows generalization to broader web navigation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/RongchangLi/WebTraveler.

deep_read.connection: 解读：规划器的证据充分性检查、结构化轨迹和逐步反思，可作为智能运维中跨手册检索与操作记录设计的参考，也可启发可靠性研究关注信息遗漏和重复决策。不过论文评测对象是网页任务，资料没有显示其在运维系统、结构设计或工程可靠性场景中的直接验证。[P4][P9]

core.title: VISTA: Structure-Aware Training-Free Editable Diagram Generation from Natural Language
core.abstract: Editable diagram generation from natural language requires structural correctness and visual readability. Text-to-image models produce rasters with no editable objects. LLM code-generation approaches yield editable output but face three challenges: unreliable geometry from token-by-token coordinate emission, shallow verification that checks code rather than the rendered image, and dependence on task-specific fine-tuning. We present VISTA, a training-free pipeline that assigns each subproblem to the appropriate component: an LLM extracts semantic structure, a deterministic algorithm computes all geometry, and a VLM inspects the rendered diagram jointly with its source and issues localized repairs. We construct a 150-prompt benchmark from PNG-only references and evaluate against eight baselines including Codex, Claude Code, and a fine-tuned multi-agent system. VISTA achieves the highest readability across all pairwise comparisons. Code and data are available at https://github.com/nice-grp/Vista.

core.title: VideoAgent: All-in-One Framework for Video Understanding and Editing
core.abstract: Video editing has become essential in digital media creation, yet existing automated systems are restricted to short segment processing and domain-specific tasks. They face two critical limitations: i) inability to handle diverse video comprehension and editing operations, and ii) lack of long-video understanding for coherent narrative creation. We propose VideoAgent, an all-in-one agentic framework addressing these challenges through two key innovations. First, we develop automated video shot creation with shot planning agents for coherent narratives and cross-modal retrieval for aligned visual content. Second, we design a multi-agent orchestration framework integrating over thirty specialized editing agents. Intent parsing filters relevant tools while textual-gradient graph optimization assembles complex editing pipelines. Extensive experiments on our newly proposed VideoEdit benchmark and public datasets demonstrate VideoAgent’s superiority over existing multimodal LLMs and agentic systems. VideoAgent achieves 87-95% orchestration success rates while reducing API costs by 60%. Human evaluation across six video categories shows that VideoAgent produces professional-quality content approaching human-level performance, with ratings only 4% below human-created videos.

article.lead: 如何让自动视频系统既能处理多样的编辑操作，又能理解长视频并形成连贯叙事？VideoAgent 尝试把镜头创作与多智能体编排结合起来，为理解复杂视频编辑任务提供了一个观察视角。

paragraphs: 视频编辑已成为数字媒体创作的重要环节，但摘要指出，现有自动化系统往往局限于短片段处理和特定领域任务。面对多样的视频理解与编辑操作，以及需要长视频理解的连贯叙事创作，这些系统仍有局限。

sections.title: 镜头创作与编辑智能体编排
paragraphs: VideoAgent 是一个一体化智能体框架。摘要描述了自动视频镜头创作：镜头规划智能体用于形成连贯叙事，跨模态检索用于获取与之对齐的视觉内容。

core.title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Assessing Exploitability of Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
core.abstract: The software supply chain has become an increasingly exposed attack surface because of its reliance on intricate yet fragile dependencies. Existing defenses such as GitHub Dependabot often raise many false alerts because their coarse-grained matching cannot determine whether a vulnerable dependency is actually exploitable. Security analysts typically spend substantial time assessing vulnerability exploitability case by case. Recent LLM agents have emerged as promising candidates for this task given their advanced capabilities in coding and cybersecurity, yet no existing benchmark evaluates them on it. Prior benchmarks target zero-day settings, where agents detect and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities. In contrast, software supply chain security focuses on how known vulnerabilities in upstream dependencies affect downstream projects. This requires agents to reason across repositories and determine whether an upstream vulnerability is exploitable in the downstream project. To address this gap, we introduce VEX-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents’ ability to assess the exploitability of software supply chain vulnerabilities. It contains 75 real-world cases mined from GitHub and labeled by security experts, covering Python, Java, and Go. We evaluate nine models across three agent harnesses. While GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 reach approximately 80% F1 on binary vulnerability-status classification, only GPT-5.5 surpasses 70% macro-F1 on fine-grained justification classification. This gap highlights the challenge of moving beyond binary exploitability assessment to identifying fine-grained exploitability reasons. Code and data: https://github.com/steven1518/vex-bench
core.summary: 【摘要】论文研究大语言模型智能体能否判断上游依赖中的已知漏洞是否影响下游项目。作者提出 VEX-Bench，收集 75 个由安全专家标注的 GitHub 真实案例，覆盖 Python、Java 和 Go，并在三种智能体运行框架下评测九个模型。摘要报告，部分模型的二元漏洞状态分类 F1 约为 80%，但细粒度理由分类仍更具挑战。当前仅依据摘要，无法核查数据划分、标注细节及完整实验结果。[摘要]

sections.title: 从依赖漏洞告警到下游可利用性
paragraphs: 软件供应链依赖复杂而脆弱，攻击面随之扩大。摘要指出，GitHub Dependabot 等现有防御工具的粗粒度匹配难以判断漏洞依赖是否真的可被利用，因此常产生大量误报；安全分析人员则需要逐案花费大量时间进行评估。
这一问题不同于侧重发现和利用未知漏洞的零日漏洞评测：供应链安全关注的是上游依赖中的已知漏洞如何影响下游项目。智能体不仅要识别漏洞，还需要跨仓库推理，判断它在具体下游项目中是否可被利用。

paragraphs: 摘要给出了案例总数、来源和语言覆盖范围，但未说明案例在各语言或漏洞类型之间的分布，也未交代专家标注的一致性。仅凭这些信息，难以判断样本对更广泛软件项目的代表性。

papers.title: What Makes Agent Memory Useful for Reliable Unanswerable Question Handling?
papers.abstract: Reliable handling of unanswerable questions (UAQs) is critical for trustworthy LLM-based agents. Although memory is widely used in agent systems, its role in reliable UAQ handling remains unclear. We present a systematic study of agent memory for UAQ handling under a unified agentic RAG framework, evaluating four representative memory methods across three UAQ-related datasets and two base models.We find that memory can improve UAQ performance in some settings, but such gains are selective rather than universal and remain fragile under dataset shift. Interestingly, cross-model memory reuse is often more feasible than cross-dataset transfer, suggesting that shifts in answerability patterns pose a greater challenge to memory reuse than changes in the base model itself. We further find that UAQ gains are more strongly preserved through decision guidance than through trajectory shaping, and that memory effectiveness depends strongly on representation. In particular, procedural and rule-based memories often provide the most reliable support for UAQ handling, while memory composition is most effective when procedural guidance is combined with complementary behavioral signals. Overall, our findings suggest that reliable UAQ memory depends less on storing larger amounts of experience and more on preserving transferable behavioral guidance.

papers.title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
papers.abstract: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization, with 2-3 times AUC improvements over reinforcement-learning and genetic-algorithm baselines on the PMO benchmark and similar gains on protein-targeted docking benchmarks. We investigate whether these gains reflect genuine optimization or benchmark artifacts, by re-evaluating a representative LLM agent under controlled blinding protocols and against a trivial random-walk baseline. We find that on PMO at the 50-call budget, the agent’s apparent advantage collapses below classical baselines once task names and curated reference compounds are removed from its prompt; a 2 times 2 ablation shows that retrieval from a small reference dictionary, not iterative optimization, is the dominant driver of the headline number. On a new protein-targeted lead-optimization benchmark with an AutoDock Vina composite oracle, a single-edit halogen/methyl random-walk mutator outperforms the LLM agent, a graph-based GA, and a non-iterative GPT baseline on every aggregate metric—a property of the oracle landscape under tight budgets, not of LLM agents per se. We release both protocols (name-blinded PMO scoring; random-walk lower bound for Vina-based protein benchmarks) as standard sanity checks for future LLM-agent papers in molecular optimization.

papers.title: WebTraveler: A Multi-Agent Framework for Continuous Exploration in Website Traversal
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as web-facing agents for information-seeking tasks over live websites. Many such tasks require multi-step in-site navigation and cross-page evidence aggregation, a setting known as web traversal. Existing LLM-based web agents, including recent explore–critic architectures, typically store interaction history as an ever-growing unstructured text trace and mix high-level planning with low-level page actions. This makes long-horizon behavior brittle, obscures the source of evidence, and often leads to redundant browsing or premature stopping. To mitigate these issues, we propose WebTraveler, a hierarchical multi-agent framework that separates high-level information-seeking planning from local web exploration and maintains a structured trajectory memory of decision-relevant signals. This design provides compact information interfaces for evidence sufficiency checking and webpage navigation, improving long-horizon stability and cross-page evidence aggregation. To obtain scalable supervision, we further introduce path-guided data synthesis, which uses executable navigation paths to collect trajectories, removes explicit path hints, and filters invalid samples through answer-consistency checks. Experiments show that WebTraveler consistently outperforms previous methods across LLM scales, especially on tasks requiring deeper navigation, with further gains from path-guided supervision. Moreover, WebTraveler also shows generalization to broader web navigation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/RongchangLi/WebTraveler.

papers.title: VISTA: Structure-Aware Training-Free Editable Diagram Generation from Natural Language
papers.abstract: Editable diagram generation from natural language requires structural correctness and visual readability. Text-to-image models produce rasters with no editable objects. LLM code-generation approaches yield editable output but face three challenges: unreliable geometry from token-by-token coordinate emission, shallow verification that checks code rather than the rendered image, and dependence on task-specific fine-tuning. We present VISTA, a training-free pipeline that assigns each subproblem to the appropriate component: an LLM extracts semantic structure, a deterministic algorithm computes all geometry, and a VLM inspects the rendered diagram jointly with its source and issues localized repairs. We construct a 150-prompt benchmark from PNG-only references and evaluate against eight baselines including Codex, Claude Code, and a fine-tuned multi-agent system. VISTA achieves the highest readability across all pairwise comparisons. Code and data are available at https://github.com/nice-grp/Vista.

papers.title: VideoAgent: All-in-One Framework for Video Understanding and Editing
papers.abstract: Video editing has become essential in digital media creation, yet existing automated systems are restricted to short segment processing and domain-specific tasks. They face two critical limitations: i) inability to handle diverse video comprehension and editing operations, and ii) lack of long-video understanding for coherent narrative creation. We propose VideoAgent, an all-in-one agentic framework addressing these challenges through two key innovations. First, we develop automated video shot creation with shot planning agents for coherent narratives and cross-modal retrieval for aligned visual content. Second, we design a multi-agent orchestration framework integrating over thirty specialized editing agents. Intent parsing filters relevant tools while textual-gradient graph optimization assembles complex editing pipelines. Extensive experiments on our newly proposed VideoEdit benchmark and public datasets demonstrate VideoAgent’s superiority over existing multimodal LLMs and agentic systems. VideoAgent achieves 87-95% orchestration success rates while reducing API costs by 60%. Human evaluation across six video categories shows that VideoAgent produces professional-quality content approaching human-level performance, with ratings only 4% below human-created videos.

papers.title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Assessing Exploitability of Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: The software supply chain has become an increasingly exposed attack surface because of its reliance on intricate yet fragile dependencies. Existing defenses such as GitHub Dependabot often raise many false alerts because their coarse-grained matching cannot determine whether a vulnerable dependency is actually exploitable. Security analysts typically spend substantial time assessing vulnerability exploitability case by case. Recent LLM agents have emerged as promising candidates for this task given their advanced capabilities in coding and cybersecurity, yet no existing benchmark evaluates them on it. Prior benchmarks target zero-day settings, where agents detect and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities. In contrast, software supply chain security focuses on how known vulnerabilities in upstream dependencies affect downstream projects. This requires agents to reason across repositories and determine whether an upstream vulnerability is exploitable in the downstream project. To address this gap, we introduce VEX-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents’ ability to assess the exploitability of software supply chain vulnerabilities. It contains 75 real-world cases mined from GitHub and labeled by security experts, covering Python, Java, and Go. We evaluate nine models across three agent harnesses. While GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 reach approximately 80% F1 on binary vulnerability-status classification, only GPT-5.5 surpasses 70% macro-F1 on fine-grained justification classification. This gap highlights the challenge of moving beyond binary exploitability assessment to identifying fine-grained exploitability reasons. Code and data: https://github.com/steven1518/vex-bench

sections.title: 从依赖漏洞告警到下游可利用性
paragraphs: 软件供应链依赖复杂而脆弱，攻击面随之扩大。摘要指出，GitHub Dependabot 等现有防御工具的粗粒度匹配难以判断漏洞依赖是否真的可被利用，因此常产生大量误报；安全分析人员则需要逐案花费大量时间进行评估。
这一问题不同于侧重发现和利用未知漏洞的零日漏洞评测：供应链安全关注的是上游依赖中的已知漏洞如何影响下游项目。智能体不仅要识别漏洞，还需要跨仓库推理，判断它在具体下游项目中是否可被利用。

sections.title: 用真实案例评估跨仓库判断
paragraphs: 作者提出 VEX-Bench，评估大语言模型智能体对软件供应链漏洞可利用性的判断能力。基准包含从 GitHub 挖掘、由安全专家标注的 75 个真实案例，覆盖 Python、Java 和 Go。
研究在三种智能体运行框架下评估了九个模型，报告了二元漏洞状态分类与细粒度理由分类的表现。摘要未进一步说明案例构建、标注细则或各运行框架的具体配置。

sections.title: 判断漏洞状态，仍难解释具体原因
paragraphs: 在二元漏洞状态分类中，GPT-5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.6 的 F1 均达到约 80%；但在细粒度理由分类中，只有 GPT-5.5 的 macro-F1 超过 70%。
这组结果表明，在所报告的评测中，从判断漏洞状态走向识别细粒度可利用性原因仍有挑战。摘要没有提供全部模型的逐项结果，因此不能据此推断其他模型之间的完整排序。

sections.title: 摘要尚不足以界定的评测范围
paragraphs: 摘要给出了案例总数、来源和语言覆盖范围，但未说明案例在各语言或漏洞类型之间的分布，也未交代专家标注的一致性。仅凭这些信息，难以判断样本对更广泛软件项目的代表性。
摘要也未详细报告模型与运行框架之间的逐项比较、具体评测设置，以及基准之外的验证范围。因此，所列分数应理解为摘要报告的基准结果，而非已经证明智能体在所有实际场景中的表现。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把结论与理由分开审视
paragraphs: 阅读启发：关注大语言模型智能体用于安全分析时，不妨同时追问它是否判断对了漏洞状态，以及给出的可利用性理由是否准确。进一步阅读时，可留意原文如何定义细粒度理由、组织跨仓库信息，并比较不同运行框架下的结果。
